newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise in average trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise in average trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares showed a flicker of life and rose on Thursday, ending a fortnight of price slippages.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index notched up 2.07 points to 335.18. Prices had ended lower all last week and the level on Tuesday was the bourse's lowest since mid-January.
The bourse on Wednesday was closed to mark Egypt's 1952 revolution.

One broker expressed cautious optimism and said investors were fishing for low priced shares. "The market has moved but not necessarily turned," said Tareq Lotfy of Intercapital. "It's a case of some foreign and local institutions bottom-fishing.
"We've had days like this before when it has risen slightly and then fallen again. I would like to see it sustained."
Turnover on Thursday was 47 million pounds ($14 million).
"The volume was relatively healthy. People are still thinking about what they are doing," Lotfy said.
Of the 78 shares traded, 20 ended lower and 44 rose in a range of sectors.
More than 5 million pounds worth of Egyptians Abroad for Investment and Development changed hands. The price fell 1.45 to 29.85.
Commercial International Bank/CIB rose a slight 0.9 pound to 69.6 pounds in 4.8 million pounds trade.
Egyptian Financial and Industrial shares got an 8 pound shot in the arm, closing at 200 in 4 million pounds trade.
Suez Cement shares inched up 0.65 pounds to 66.65.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 450.58 points from 448.19 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 250.18 points from 248.52.
